source.subject: Science
source.extractionPreview:
Motion and Time
9
I
n Class VI, you learnt about different
types of motions. You learnt that a
motion could be along a straight line,
it could be circular or periodic. Can you
recall these three types of motions?
Table 9.1 gives some common
examples of motions. Identify the type
of motion in each case.
9.1 SLOW OR FAST
We know that some vehicles move faster
than others. Even the same vehicle may
move faster or slower at different times.
Make a list of ten objects moving along
a straight path. Gr

activities.question: Compare two important ideas from Chapter 9.
activities.instructions: Use the source-based options to complete this activity.

correctItems.text: Make a list of ten objects moving along a straight path.
How did you decide which object is moving slow and which one is moving fast?

Let us look at the motion of vehicles moving on a road.

activities.question: Arrange key steps or ideas from Chapter 9 in order.

correctItems.text: The distance covered by you after 5 minutes would be much smaller than that covered by the bus.
Would you say that the bus is moving faster than the bicycle?
We often say that the faster vehicle has a higher speed.
In a 100-metre race it is easy to decide whose speed is the highest.

correctItems.text: One who takes shortest time to cover the distance of 100 metres has the highest speed.

In the examples given above, a higher speed seems to indicate that a given distance has been covered in a shorter time, or a larger distance covered in a given time.
The most convenient way to find out which of the two or more objects is moving faster is to compare the distances moved by them in a unit time.

activities.question: Write a short answer using key points from Chapter 9.
activities.instructions: Place the options in the correct placeholders. The sentence order must match the answer key.

correctItems.text: One who takes shortest time to cover the distance of 100 metres has the highest speed.
9.2 SPEED You are probably familiar with the word speed.
In the examples given above, a higher speed seems to indicate that a given distance has been covered in a shorter time, or a larger distance covered in a given time.
The most convenient way to find out which of the two or more objects is moving faster is to compare the distances moved by them in a unit time.
